harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service (inventory-api.service) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and running on port 8080 via $NODE_IP. Verified the kernel's global OOM killer, when driven out of memory by an unprotected memory-hog process (oom_score_adj=0), selects and kills the hog while inventory-api keeps serving without interruption (same PID before/after). Confirmed this behavior both before and after a full node reboot, and proved the reboot actually occurred via a changed boot_id and fresh uptime.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: Ubuntu 24.04, 1.9GiB RAM, no swap, python3 available
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-api.py, a threaded HTTP JSON service on port 8080
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, Restart=always, enabled at boot
Wrote /usr/local/bin/memory-hog.py, an unbounded memory-consuming script
Started inventory-api and verified active state, PID, oom_score_adj=-1000, and successful curl
Launched memory-hog as a transient systemd unit (memory-hog.service) with default oom_score_adj=0
Polled memory usage and dmesg until the kernel's global OOM killer fired
Confirmed dmesg shows 'Out of memory: Killed process ... (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0' targeting the hog, while inventory-api remained active with unchanged PID and uptime growing
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service health baseline
Issued 'sudo -n systemctl reboot' on node1; acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Verified boot_id changed and uptime reflects a fresh boot
Verified inventory-api auto-started (enabled), correct oom_score_adj=-1000, and served a request post-reboot
Re-ran the memory-hog OOM scenario post-reboot to confirm the protection persists across restart: kernel again killed the hog, inventory-api stayed active throughout

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (systemd) service on node1
evidence.summary: Unit created, enabled, active; MainPID reported by systemctl; curl returns valid JSON response

evidence.requirement: inventory-api is protected from the OOM killer (oom_score_adj=-1000)
evidence.summary: systemctl show reports OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 and /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj confirms -1000

evidence.requirement: Under real system memory pressure, the kernel OOM killer stops the memory-hog process, not inventory-api
evidence.summary: Memory hog launched with oom_score_adj=0; dmesg shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 1315 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0'; inventory-api (pid 1285) remained active the entire time with growing uptime and a successful curl response after the kill; free -h shows memory reclaimed

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity capture on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45, confirmed inventory-api active+enabled and serving via curl

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued and returned exit_code 0 before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Immediate poll failed with connection reset (node down), next poll succeeded with new boot_id d409655a-9797-475d-a310-6e7931adf86d, differing from the pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of inventory-api and re-verification of OOM protection
evidence.summary: Fresh uptime confirms new boot; inventory-api active/enabled with new PID 649, oom_score_adj=-1000, serving curl; re-ran the memory-hog scenario post-reboot and dmesg again shows the kernel killing the unprotected hog (pid 893) while inventory-api (pid 649) stayed active and kept serving throughout
